newsitem.title: GERMANY: Meister says monetary policy can't create jobs.
newsitem.headline: Meister says monetary policy can't create jobs.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister said that problems on the jobless market could not be resolved through monetary policy and certainly not by government interference in monetary policy.

"Problems on the jobs market cannot be solved via monetary policy, via stronger influence of governments on monetary policy or via exchange rate policies," he said, according to the text of a speech for a conference in Austria.
"As the experience of several countries in the past has shown, attempts of this type can have short-term effects at best," he said.
He added: "The euro is not a miracle weapon which can correct the mistakes of the past."
Instead, job market problems must be addressed by hitting at the root of the problems, he said. This meant breaking down structural barriers and rigidities in the workplace, he said.
